keyframe_review.note: 143,936 km2 (449 cells): Johor, Pahang, Kelantan, Terengganu, Perak, Selangor, Negeri Sembilan, Melaka, southern Thailand (Pattani, Yala, Narathiwat, part of Songkhla) and the Singapore cells; Kedah has its own Cliopatria row and Nakhon Si Thammarat is outside. No page names a state with this outline: the Malaya page is a disambiguation, the History of Malaysia page has 'By the late 13th century, the Siamese kings of Sukhothai had brought most of Malaya under their rule' and the Tambralinga page has Nakhon Si Thammarat a tributary of Sukhothai under the stele of 1283 (or 1292). The row is read as an aggregate of the Malay principalities of the peninsula (Pahang, Kelantan, Terengganu, Patani, Johor and others) with soft borders. Outline kept as drawn, status corrected. Infobox gives no area.

keyframe_review.note: Same 143,043 km2 outline for 1344-1351. The 1365 Nagarakretagama (opened for the Majapahit dossier) names 'Hujung Medini (and Singapore)' with Pahang, Kelantan, Johor and Kedah among the lands the Majapahit king claimed; the History of Malaysia page has Majapahit in 'possession of the peninsula' in the 14th century. Cliopatria hands the outline to Majapahit in 1352, which the Majapahit dossier draws as a tributary tint.

region.text: the Malay Peninsula south of Nakhon Si Thammarat, without Kedah

ledger.note: 1294: the Malay principalities of the peninsula appear in Cliopatria. The row is the Malay Peninsula land of Srivijaya's last shape (403 cells; the srivijaya dossier names malaya a successor). The History of Malaysia page: 'By the late 13th century, the Siamese kings of Sukhothai had brought most of Malaya under their rule', and Srivijaya's last ruler was 'conquered and overthrown in 1288'. No page gives a state called Malaya, so the year and the outline are Cliopatria's.

c. 1299: Singapore island is Singapura's. Infobox of the Kingdom of Singapura page 'Founding of Temasek by Sang Nila Utama: 1299'; Cliopatria takes the two island cells out of Malaya in 1305. (The History of Malaysia page dates the founding to 1324.)

1351: the peninsula passes to Majapahit's sphere. 'In the 14th century, the Hindu Majapahit Empire came into possession of the peninsula' (undated); the 1365 Nagarakretagama lists Pahang, Kelantan, Johor and Kedah. Cliopatria's Majapahit shape of 1352 holds 445 of the Malaya cells; the Majapahit dossier draws them as a tributary tint (1352-1406) because direct rule 'did not extend beyond east Java and Bali'.

notes:
WHAT 'MALAYA' IS. The Wikipedia article 'Malaya' is a disambiguation page (British Malaya, Malayan Union, Federation of Malaya 1948-1963, Peninsular Malaysia), and Wikidata Q1479726 is shared with the Federation of Malaya: the two Cliopatria rows are DIFFERENT states (Malaya 1294-1351 and Federation of Malaya 1958-1962); only the Wikidata id is the same. The 1294-1351 row is a catch-all for the Malay principalities of the peninsula (Pahang, Kelantan, Terengganu, Patani and Langkasuka, Johor, Perak and others), about 143,000 km2, with no state of this name and no capital in any source opened. The dossier keeps the outline (a drawing of 'the Malay lands' with soft borders, no capital) and corrects its status; the right fix is to replace it by dossiers for the individual principalities. A gap-filler should open the articles on Pahang, Kelantan, Terengganu, Patani, Langkasuka and the Sukhothai Kingdom (the Ram Khamhaeng stele's southern vassals) and decide whether 'most of Malaya' was Sukhothai's tributary tint in 1294-1351 (the History of Malaysia page says so for the late 13th century; the sukhothai-kingdom dossier records the south leaving c. 1300).

Disagreement between pages: Singapura is founded c. 1299 (Kingdom of Singapura page) or 1324 (History of Malaysia).

PAGE BUDGET (1-2): the Malaya page (a disambiguation, thin), Tambralinga, History of Malaysia, with the Nagarakretagama and Kingdom of Singapura pages shared from other dossiers: five listed, two more than the budget because the first yielded nothing. Not opened: Sukhothai Kingdom, Pahang, Kelantan, Terengganu, Patani, Langkasuka. Infobox: none (disambiguation page), so no area could be compared. capitals is empty because no source names a seat.
